claim_verdicts.evidence: Round 2: lesson sec. 4 now reads 'OpenTelemetry stores and shows nothing', matching the ledger. opentelemetry.io: "OpenTelemetry is not an observability backend itself." "The backend (storage) and the frontend (visualization) of telemetry data are intentionally left to other tools." Components listed: APIs, "Language SDKs", OTLP.

"OpenTelemetry uses alternate terms 'Tracer' and 'Span'. In .NET 'ActivitySource' is the implementation of Tracer and Activity is the implementation of 'Span'." Since the .NET types implement the tracing API, libraries call them rather than an OpenTelemetry package (round-2 addition in sec. 3 follows from this).

OTel .NET: "The name of each ActivitySource must match a name passed to AddSource when configuring the TracerProvider"; otherwise "activities created by that source aren't collected." .NET docs: "If there are no registered listeners or there are listeners that are not interested, StartActivity() will return null and avoid creating the Activity object."

Round 2: ledger now uses the round-1 suggested_text. .NET docs: "Some activities are created automatically by the platform, such as the one by ASP.NET to represent the handling of a request"; OTel sample shows ActivitySourceName Microsoft.AspNetCore. Npgsql: AddNpgsql() "activates ... Npgsql's tracing". EF Core docs list PostgreSQL provider Npgsql.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL via .UseNpgsql. trace-refund.txt shows '(5 SQL)' spans.
